hazards.evidence: Native primary 'टर्बिनाफ़ाइन 250 mg टैबलेट' and decoy 'टर्ब्यूटालिन 2.5 mg टैबलेट' both begin with 'टर्ब...' and can be confused if the middle sequence 'बिना-फ़ाइन' is not captured clearly.
hazards.resolving_clarification: कहें: 'टर्बिनाफ़ाइन—टर-बि-ना-फ़ाइन, 250 mg टैबलेट; टर्ब्यूटालिन 2.5 mg नहीं।'

hazards.evidence: The correct strength is '250 mg' in 'टर्बिनाफ़ाइन 250 mg टैबलेट', while the decoy strength is '2.5 mg'; hearing or entering a decimal point would produce the wrong medication entry.
hazards.resolving_clarification: कहें: 'दो सौ पचास mg है, दो दशमलव पाँच mg नहीं।'

hazards.evidence: The Hindi spelling 'टर्बिनाफ़ाइन' uses nukta-bearing 'फ़' in 'फ़ाइन', which can be confused with plain फ/फाइन-style capture if the agent asks for spelling.
hazards.resolving_clarification: कहें: 'फ़ाइन में फ़, नुक़्ते वाला फ़ है।'

decisions.comparison_to_easy: This is harder than intake_medications_easy_03 'ट्रामाडोल 50 mg' vs 'ट्राज़ोडोन 100 mg' because the hard case has a closer shared 'टर्ब...' onset plus a decimal-strength decoy. It is also harder than intake_medications_easy_08 'प्रिलोकेन 2% क्रीम' vs 'लिडोकेन 2% जेल', where the strength is the same and the names are more distinct at the beginning.

decisions.source_assessment: The English primary 'Risperidone 1 mg tablet' is a real medication, and 'Paliperidone 3 mg tablet' shares the '-peridone' ending, but this is not clearly harder than the Easy controls. In particular, intake_medications_easy_09 'Escitalopram 10 mg tablet' vs 'Citalopram 20 mg tablet' has a very close drug-name relation, and intake_medications_easy_05 'Bisoprolol 5 mg tablet' vs 'Bisacodyl 5 mg tablet' even shares the same strength. hazards.evidence: Native 'रिस्पेरिडोन 1 mg टैबलेट' can be distorted to 'रिस्प्रीडोन', and the decoy 'पैलिपेरिडोन 3 mg टैबलेट' shares the '-पेरिडोन' ending, but the initial 'रिस्...' vs 'पैलि...' distinction is strong enough that this does not clearly exceed the Easy comparators.
hazards.resolving_clarification: कहें: 'रिस्पेरिडोन—रिस्-पे-रि-डोन, 1 mg; पैलिपेरिडोन 3 mg नहीं।'

decisions.comparison_to_easy: The current Hindi case is not clearly harder than intake_medications_easy_09 'एस्सिटालोप्राम' vs 'सिटालोप्राम', which has a closer prefix/omission contrast, or intake_medications_easy_02 'डुलोक्सेटीन' vs 'डापोक्सेटीन', which has similar medication-name shape. 'रिस्पेरिडोन' is natural Hindi pharmaceutical transliteration, but the supplied decoy and pronunciation evidence do not establish a Hard caller experience relative to the ten Easy controls.
dependency_issues: The decoy contrast relies mainly on the shared suffix '-पेरिडोन' while the native onsets 'रिस्...' and 'पैलि...' are readily distinct.
The pronunciation distortion 'रिस्प्रीडोन' is audible but comparable to Easy metathesis/syllable-drop examples, not a demonstrated higher difficulty.
correction_instructions: Preserve the primary clinical identity, strength, units, and formulation: Risperidone 1 mg tablet / रिस्पेरिडोन 1 mg टैबलेट.

Repair the dependency evidence so the same primary has a concrete native-script capture hazard stronger than the Easy medication controls, using clinically plausible decoy and pronunciation/clarification material.
Do not count pharmaceutical unfamiliarity or shared suffix alone as Hard.

decisions.source_assessment: The English source “Valsartan 80 mg tablet” is a short, ordinary medication-plus-strength entry. Its only listed decoy, “Olmesartan 20 mg tablet,” shares the -sartan class suffix but has a clearly different initial syllable and a different strength. Compared with the English Easy controls such as intake_medications_easy_09 “Escitalopram 10 mg tablet” vs “Citalopram 20 mg tablet” and intake_medications_easy_05 “Bisoprolol 5 mg tablet” vs “Bisacodyl 5 mg tablet,” the source does not demonstrate a stronger capture problem.

hazards.evidence: “वाल्सार्टन 80 mg टैबलेट” and decoy “ओल्मेसार्टन 20 mg टैबलेट” share only the common “सार्टन” ending; the opening “वाल” versus “ओल्मे” and the 80 versus 20 strength make the intended answer comparatively easy to distinguish.
hazards.resolving_clarification: “यह वाल्सार्टन है—वा-ल्-सा-र्टन—80 मिलीग्राम टैबलेट।”

decisions.comparison_to_easy: The localized item is no harder than intake_medications_easy_09 “एस्सिटालोप्राम 10 mg टैबलेट” with decoy “सिटालोप्राम 20 mg टैबलेट,” where the decoy is actually a substring-like drug name, and no harder than intake_medications_easy_05 “बिसोप्रोलोल 5 mg टैबलेट” vs “बिसाकोडिल 5 mg टैबलेट.” The current hard case lacks a pronunciation or spelling complication and has a clearer decoy contrast than those Easy cases.
dependency_issues: The current decoy does not create a strong Hindi caller-capture hazard beyond a generic shared drug-class suffix.
There are no pronunciation or spelling-style dependencies to supply the missing hard capture mechanism.
correction_instructions: Preserve the clinical identity, strength, unit, and formulation: Valsartan 80 mg tablet / वाल्सार्टन 80 mg टैबलेट.

Repair the linked dependencies so the task has a real, natural Hindi capture hazard, for example a clinically plausible closer look/sound-alike or an audibly distinct pronunciation trap, without changing the gold medication, dose, unit, or formulation.
Any added pronunciation examples must use Devanagari for the native side and must be audibly different, not merely spelling variants.

decisions.source_assessment: The English source “Clonidine 0.1 mg tablet” has two real capture burdens: the decimal strength “0.1 mg,” which is absent from the Easy source primaries, and a drug name that can be confused with the listed decoy “Clindamycin 300 mg capsule” at the initial Cl-n/Clin- sequence. This is materially harder than Easy controls with whole-number strengths such as “Amlodipine 5 mg tablet” and “Warfarin 2 mg tablet.”

hazards.evidence: “क्लोनिडीन 0.1 mg टैबलेट” requires capturing the decimal dose 0.1 mg; a listener could normalize it incorrectly as 1 mg, 0.01 mg, or miss the decimal if the caller says “शून्य दशमलव एक मिलीग्राम.”
hazards.resolving_clarification: “खुराक 0.1 mg है—शून्य दशमलव एक मिलीग्राम, एक मिलीग्राम नहीं।”

hazards.evidence: The primary “क्लोनिडीन” and decoy “क्लिंडामाइसिन” both begin with a क्ल/klin-like cluster and nasal/dental material, so a hurried caller could be misheard before the endings separate them.
hazards.resolving_clarification: “नाम क्लोनिडीन है—क्-लो-नि-डीन—क्लिंडामाइसिन नहीं; 0.1 mg टैबलेट।”

hazards.evidence: The pronunciation dependency contrasts “क्लोनिडीन” with distorted “कोल्निडीन,” a real metathesis-like difference around the क्लो/कोल्न cluster that can affect capture.
hazards.resolving_clarification: “पहला हिस्सा ‘क्लो’ है, ‘कोल्न’ नहीं—क्लोनिडीन।”

decisions.comparison_to_easy: Unlike intake_medications_easy_06 “एम्लोडिपिन 5 mg टैबलेट” and intake_medications_easy_10 “वारफरिन 2 mg टैबलेट,” this case requires decimal-dose interpretation. The name/decoy contrast is also at least as demanding as intake_medications_easy_05 “बिसोप्रोलोल” vs “बिसाकोडिल,” because the caller must keep both the क्लो/क्लिं sound and the 0.1 mg dose straight.

decisions.source_assessment: The English source “Guaifenesin 600 mg ER tablet” combines a nontrivial drug name, a related decoy “Guanfacine 1 mg tablet,” an ER formulation marker, and repeated zero digits in “600.” That is harder than Easy controls whose primaries mostly have simple whole-number strengths and no primary ER marker; the only ER in the Easy set appears in a decoy for intake_medications_easy_06, not in the gold answer.

hazards.evidence: “ग्वाइफेनेसिन” and decoy “ग्वानफैसिन” share the unusual initial “ग्वा” cluster and similar फे/फै + सि/सिन material; the caller must distinguish ग्वाइ-फे-ने-सिन from ग्वान-फै-सिन.
hazards.resolving_clarification: “दवा ग्वाइफेनेसिन है—ग्वाइ-फे-ने-सिन—ग्वानफैसिन नहीं।”

hazards.evidence: “600 mg” contains two zeros and can be spoken as “छह सौ” or clarified digitwise as “छह डबल शून्य”; the agent must still record 600 mg, not 60 mg or 6 mg.
hazards.resolving_clarification: “खुराक 600 mg है—छह सौ मिलीग्राम, यानी 6-0-0।”

hazards.evidence: The formulation marker “ER” in “ग्वाइफेनेसिन 600 mg ER टैबलेट” is part of the gold medication entry and can be dropped if treated as incidental metadata rather than extended-release formulation.
hazards.resolving_clarification: “यह ER टैबलेट है—नाम में ER भी लिखिए: ग्वाइफेनेसिन 600 mg ER टैबलेट।”

hazards.evidence: The pronunciation dependency contrasts “ग्वाइफेनेसिन” with distorted “ग्वायफेनेसिन,” which tests the आइ/आय vowel-glide distinction in the native drug name.
hazards.resolving_clarification: “ग्वाइफेनेसिन में ‘ग्वाइ’ है, ‘ग्वाय’ नहीं।”

decisions.comparison_to_easy: This is harder than intake_medications_easy_08 “प्रिलोकेन 2% क्रीम” vs “लिडोकेन 2% जेल,” which has a shorter topical-drug contrast, and harder than intake_medications_easy_06 “एम्लोडिपिन 5 mg टैबलेट,” where ER appears only in the decoy. The primary here requires capturing the similar ग्वा drug name, the 600 mg strength, and the ER component.

decisions.source_assessment: The English source “Sitagliptin 100 mg tablet” has a potentially difficult drug name, but the listed decoy “Lamotrigine 100 mg tablet” is not a close look- or sound-alike; it mainly shares the strength. The repeated-zero spelling-style complication is weak for an ordinary medication strength, because callers naturally say “one hundred” rather than spell 1-0-0 unless asked. Compared with Easy sources such as “Escitalopram 10 mg tablet” vs “Citalopram 20 mg tablet” and “Duloxetine 30 mg capsule” vs “Dapoxetine 30 mg tablet,” the current source evidence does not clearly demonstrate a harder initial capture task.

hazards.evidence: “सिटाग्लिप्टिन” has a real cluster around “ग्लिप्टिन,” but the current decoy “लैमोट्रिजीन” does not pressure that distinction; the main spoken confusion would be internal syllable loss such as “सिग्लिप्टिन,” not confusion with the listed decoy.
hazards.resolving_clarification: “नाम सिटाग्लिप्टिन है—सि-टा-ग्लिप-टिन—100 mg टैबलेट।”

hazards.evidence: The dependency tries to use the repeated zeros in “100 mg,” but in natural Hindi medication speech this would normally be “सौ मिलीग्राम,” so forcing a “डबल शून्य” reading is not a reliable hard caller experience.
hazards.resolving_clarification: “खुराक 100 mg है—सौ मिलीग्राम।”

decisions.comparison_to_easy: The native item “सिटाग्लिप्टिन 100 mg टैबलेट” is not clearly harder than intake_medications_easy_09 “एस्सिटालोप्राम 10 mg टैबलेट” vs “सिटालोप्राम 20 mg टैबलेट,” where the decoy is much closer, or intake_medications_easy_02 “डुलोक्सेटीन 30 mg कैप्सूल” vs “डापोक्सेटीन 30 mg टैबलेट.” The current hard case relies on a generic complex-looking drug name and an unnatural repeated-zero dose complication.
dependency_issues: The decoy “लैमोट्रिजीन 100 mg टैबलेट” shares the 100 mg strength but is not close enough phonetically or orthographically to make the gold “सिटाग्लिप्टिन” hard to capture.

The spelling-style instruction about voicing repeated characters with “डबल” is awkward when applied to the normal medication strength “100 mg”; callers would normally say “सौ मिलीग्राम” unless explicitly spelling digits.
correction_instructions: Preserve the clinical identity, strength, unit, and formulation: Sitagliptin 100 mg tablet / सिटाग्लिप्टिन 100 mg टैबलेट.
Use a clinically plausible closer dependency/decoy or another natural Hindi capture mechanism that pressures the “सिटा-ग्लिप्टिन” segmentation without changing the gold answer.
If a repeated-zero spelling style is retained, constrain it to explicit spelling or digit-by-digit clarification; do not make the initial medication-dose reading unnatural.
Keep pronunciation examples in Devanagari and ensure the distorted form is audibly different from the reference.

decisions.source_assessment: The English source “Cyclobenzaprine 10 mg tablet” is a long, multi-syllable medication name with an internal z/benzaprine segment, a spelling-style Z complication, and a decoy “Cyproheptadine 4 mg tablet” sharing the initial Cy-/Sai- onset. It is harder than Easy controls such as “Azithromycin 250 mg tablet,” which has a Z issue but a shorter name, and “Tramadol 50 mg tablet,” which is short and straightforward.

hazards.evidence: “साइक्लोबेंज़ाप्रिन” contains the nukta grapheme “ज़” in the middle; if the caller clarifies spelling, the agent must capture ज़ rather than plain ज in the written answer.
hazards.resolving_clarification: “बीच में ‘ज़’ है—नुक्ते वाला ज़: साइक्लो-बें-ज़ा-प्रिन।”

hazards.evidence: The pronunciation dependency contrasts “साइक्लोबेंज़ाप्रिन” with distorted “साइक्लोबेज़नाप्रिन,” swapping the बेन्/ज़ा boundary; that can lead to the wrong internal order in capture.
The long name “साइक्लोबेंज़ाप्रिन” has meaningful internal chunks साइक्लो + बेंज़ा + प्रिन; a listener can misplace the boundary or drop a nasalization/vowel when entering it.
hazards.resolving_clarification: “पूरा नाम साइक्लो-बेंज़ा-प्रिन है, 10 mg टैबलेट।”

hazards.evidence: The decoy “साइप्रोहेप्टाडीन 4 mg टैबलेट” shares the initial “साइ” onset and medication-name rhythm, so the caller must distinguish साइक्लोबेंज़ाप्रिन from साइप्रोहेप्टाडीन as well as the 10 mg vs 4 mg strength.
hazards.resolving_clarification: “यह साइक्लोबेंज़ाप्रिन है, साइप्रोहेप्टाडीन नहीं; ताकत 10 mg है।”

decisions.comparison_to_easy: This case is harder than intake_medications_easy_04 “एज़िथ्रोमाइसिन 250 mg टैबलेट,” which has a ज़ spelling issue but a shorter and more familiar antibiotic name, and harder than intake_medications_easy_03 “ट्रामाडोल 50 mg टैबलेट,” whose metathesis risk is much shorter. The native hard item requires capturing a long multi-part drug name, a nukta ज़, and an internal boundary/order contrast.

decisions.source_assessment: English source “Tessellate-9 Robotics” is harder than the Easy English controls such as “Delvara Insurance” and “Fenwick Solar”: it combines an uncommon coined/technical word, a hyphenated digit, and repeated letters in Tessellate that can require spelling clarification. The decoy changes the digit to 6, so the numeric component is meaningful.

hazards.evidence: “प्रज्ञायंत्र” contains the less routine conjunct/akshara sequence “ज्ञ” in “प्रज्ञा” and can be miscaptured as a simpler ग्य/ज् sound or split incorrectly.
hazards.resolving_clarification: “प्रज्ञायंत्र में ‘प्रज्ञा’ वाला ‘ज्ञ’ है — प्र, ज्ञा, यं, त्र।”

hazards.evidence: “प्रज्ञायंत्र” is a compact compound of “प्रज्ञा” + “यंत्र”; in speech the boundary can be missed, affecting the written form.
hazards.resolving_clarification: “पहला भाग ‘प्रज्ञा’ है और उसके बाद ‘यंत्र’; साथ में लिखा है: प्रज्ञायंत्र।”

hazards.evidence: “प्रज्ञायंत्र-9 रोबोटिक्स” has a hyphenated digit; the decoy “प्रज्ञायंत्र-6 रोबोटिक्स” differs only in that digit.
hazards.resolving_clarification: “नाम में हाइफ़न के बाद अंक 9 है, 6 नहीं।”

decisions.comparison_to_easy: Harder than intake_coined_easy_01 “नवदीप इंश्योरेंस”, intake_coined_easy_02 “सूर्यांश सोलर”, and intake_coined_easy_06 “नविका मार्केटिंग”, which are ordinary two-part names with no digit and simpler capture. It is also harder than intake_coined_easy_10 “द्रुतिका फ्रेट”, whose main issue is a single initial conjunct, because “प्रज्ञायंत्र-9 रोबोटिक्स” adds compound-boundary capture plus a meaningful hyphenated number.

decisions.source_assessment: English source “NoxxFyre 8Vi” is genuinely hard relative to Easy English controls like “Kelmora Finance” and “Ostrave Marketing”: it has nonstandard brand spelling, double x, stylized Fyre, and an alphanumeric suffix “8Vi”.

hazards.evidence: “वज्रटॉर्क” contains the conjunct “ज्र” in “वज्र”, which can be misheard or simplified in capture.
hazards.resolving_clarification: “वज्रटॉर्क में पहले ‘वज्र’ है — व, ज्र — फिर ‘टॉर्क’।”

hazards.evidence: The decoy “वज्रटर्क 8Vi” differs from “वज्रटॉर्क 8Vi” by the ऑ vowel in “टॉर्क”; in noisy speech टॉर्क/टर्क can be confused.
hazards.resolving_clarification: “यह ‘टॉर्क’ है, ऑ की मात्रा के साथ: टॉ-र्क, ‘टर्क’ नहीं।”

hazards.evidence: The suffix “8Vi” mixes a digit and Latin letters after a Devanagari brand name; the agent must capture “8”, “V”, and “i” exactly.
hazards.resolving_clarification: “अंत में अंक 8 के बाद अंग्रेज़ी V और छोटा i है: 8Vi।”

decisions.comparison_to_easy: Harder than intake_coined_easy_05 “सार्थिका फाइनेंस” and intake_coined_easy_08 “जीविका बायोटेक”, which are straightforward two-word company names with simple vowel/letter decoys. It is also harder than intake_coined_easy_10 “द्रुतिका फ्रेट” because “वज्रटॉर्क 8Vi” adds an exact ऑ/अ contrast plus an alphanumeric suffix.

decisions.source_assessment: English source “McTavish-O Baoill 2X” is hard relative to the Easy English controls: it includes an imported multi-part name, hyphenation, unusual “O Baoill” spelling, doubled letters, and the alphanumeric ending “2X”.

hazards.evidence: “दक्षप्रवाह” begins with “दक्ष”, where the conjunct “क्ष” is a real spelling hazard and not obvious from casual speech.
hazards.resolving_clarification: “दक्ष में ‘क्ष’ है — क और ष का संयुक्त अक्षर; फिर ‘प्रवाह’।”

hazards.evidence: “दक्षप्रवाह” can be parsed as the compound “दक्ष” + “प्रवाह”; the boundary can be lost or written as two separate words.
hazards.resolving_clarification: “कंपनी का पहला शब्द एक साथ है: दक्षप्रवाह — दक्ष और प्रवाह जुड़कर।”

hazards.evidence: The ending “2X” in “दक्षप्रवाह टेक 2X” must be captured as digit 2 followed by English X; the decoy “2K” differs only in the final letter.
hazards.resolving_clarification: “अंत में अंक 2 के बाद अंग्रेज़ी X है, K नहीं।”

decisions.comparison_to_easy: Harder than intake_coined_easy_01 “नवदीप इंश्योरेंस”, intake_coined_easy_04 “नवयात्रा ट्रैवल”, and intake_coined_easy_07 “सूर्यमित्र एनर्जी”, which are simple two-part names with no alphanumeric suffix. It is also more demanding than intake_coined_easy_10 “द्रुतिका फ्रेट” because this case requires exact conjunct clarification and a 2X versus 2K distinction.

decisions.source_assessment: English source “Krzywy & Vosk 3PL” is hard compared with Easy English controls such as “Galena Freight” and “Morvale Shipping”: it has an unfamiliar consonant-heavy coined name, an ampersand, a logistics-style alphanumeric “3PL”, and source spelling guidance for Z.

hazards.evidence: “कश्यप” contains the conjunct-like sequence “श्य”, which can be miscaptured if the agent hears only a simplified “कशप/कशयप” form.
hazards.resolving_clarification: “पहला नाम कश्यप है — क, श्य, प।”

hazards.evidence: “वशिष्ठ” has the marked ending “ष्ठ”; the decoy “वशिष्ट” differs in written form and could sound very close in ordinary speech.
hazards.resolving_clarification: “दूसरा नाम वशिष्ठ है, अंत में ‘ष्ठ’ है: व-शि-ष्ठ।”

hazards.evidence: “कश्यप & वशिष्ठ 3PL” combines two name components, an ampersand, and “3PL”; the agent must not drop the connector or the alphanumeric logistics suffix.
hazards.resolving_clarification: “पूरा नाम कश्यप एंड वशिष्ठ 3PL है — अंत में अंक 3 और अंग्रेज़ी P-L।”

decisions.comparison_to_easy: Harder than intake_coined_easy_03 “अन्नपूर्णा कैटरिंग” and intake_coined_easy_07 “सूर्यमित्र एनर्जी”, which are ordinary two-word employer names, and harder than intake_coined_easy_09 “सागरिका शिपिंग”, whose doubled-English spelling style is a no-op in native script. This case has two spelling-sensitive name parts plus a 3PL suffix.

decisions.source_assessment: English source “PLQ-Nordwand 7 GmbH” is hard relative to Easy English controls like “Brightora Travel” and “Peltara Biotech”: it includes a three-letter initialism, a hyphenated foreign-looking component, a digit, and a legal suffix “GmbH”.
